features.title: World Shell navigation to a tracked job opportunity, its linked draft outputs, provenance and the shared editor
features.build: The member journey works entirely from the World Shell (/world) — admin navigation is irrelevant. Member logs in (lands on /world), reaches the career opportunity pipeline from a World Shell island/entry, opens a tracked opportunity (placeholder: company + role title), sees the application-package outputs linked to it (drafts) with provenance proving they came from the member's own Career Master (source, dates, authors, version, lineage). Opens a draft in the EXISTING shared editor (HerqOutputConfigurator / OutputTemplateConfigurator — no new editor), edits, saves (new draft version), Approve for QR through useToolCategoryGate().run and assertReadyToFinalize. UI to create a placeholder opportunity and link/unlink outputs; import-application-package.mjs option to create/link the placeholder from the gitignored package JSON (never hardcode a company or role). Additive storage. Desktop + 390px. Fictional data: 'Northwind Freight', 'Principal Value Architect'.

features.title: Outputs populate from Career Master with per-output overrides; packages enter Career Master via the reconciliation queue
features.build: Career Master is the source of truth ('Career Master + overrides'). Template-driven AND imported outputs bind sections (roles, skills, tools, certifications, KPIs) to Career Master, with per-output overrides stored on the output and shown as overridden in the editor (revert per field). An imported package's differences go to the Career Reconciliation queue — accept writes to Career Master through normal CRUD, reject keeps the override. Queue reachable from the World Shell and the output editor (UI, not API-only). Approve/publish through the finalization gate.

features.title: Output version history: dates, tracked changes and a timeline slider across versions
features.build: Every output lineage (lineage_root_id) shows its full version history in the output editor and My Resume: created/modified dates per version, approver, tracked changes between any two versions (block-level diff shown inline like tracked changes), and a timeline slider scrubbing previous states with the rendered output updating. Reachable from the World Shell opportunity view and the editor.

features.build: Every rollup feeding resume outputs is editable in a UI screen ('5 · Resume rollups' in CareerExperienceConfigurator, reached from the World Shell): KPI tiles, industry buckets, skill category groups, Career Atom groupings, with live preview. Member-scoped definitions, additive. Outputs read the configured rollups; proficiency from careerProficiencyEngine.js incl. † footnotes.

Dataviz palette; append-only block registry; reachable from the World Shell.

features.title: Cover letter per opportunity, package table of contents, confined cover-letter agent
features.build: 1) Every job opportunity gets a template cover letter auto-generated against its job rec (no LLM) into its linked drafts, plus a 'Generate for this opportunity' action. 2) The printed package has a title block and numbered table of contents like the original upload (page numbers, clickable entries) and always includes the cover letter. 3) A cover-letter agent the member talks to in plain text from the package editor, reachable from the World Shell opportunity view: confined to the one letter; library search confined to that package; search + deterministic edits first; only then the cheapest model (UI setting, default claude-haiku-4-5-20251001) with search hits and only affected paragraphs, returning iterative edit operations — never a regenerated letter; tracked-changes accept/reject; accept = new draft version; per-turn LLM used/model/tokens/latency recorded; approve/publish through the finalization gate; template/model/tone editable in UI; errors surfaced.

features.title: Release reconciliation, failed-run states and contribution intelligence trends
features.build: Session, design and build outputs (change specs, training specs, test results, triage, reconciliation reports, release logs, commits) reconcile to master outputs per feature release: features, traced spec versions, validation per round, fixes, failed runs (incl. usage-limit deaths) as first-class states. Contribution trends over time: tokens and time per feature/role/release, rounds-to-pass, failure classes. Additive tables + idempotent importer (scripts/import-release-logs.mjs). Admin screen reachable from the World Shell with dated trend charts and a timeline slider.

features.title: After-session context / prompt / cache / memory mapping with token, spend and time trends
features.build: scripts/analyze-session.mjs reads Claude Code transcripts (+ subagents; message.usage counted once per message id; compactions and usage-limit errors = limit events) and in-app agent runs: tokens by type, cache-hit ratio, agents, time, limit events, spend from a UI-editable price table — metrics and mapping summary only, never transcript text. Mapping proposals into context (CLAUDE.md / skill refs), prompt (skills, workflows, agent prompts), cache (stable prefixes), memory (docs/active-universal-salt-basin-agent-memory-register.md) with evidence and suggested edits. Additive tables; 'Sessions' screen from the World Shell (admin) with mapping queue and dated trends (one axis per chart, timeline slider, before/after of applied mappings). Non-blocking SessionEnd hook in .claude/settings.json plus the in-app agent completion path.

features.title: World Shell layered navigation: the sun crystal is the root menu and every click moves one layer deeper, with more detail on each object
features.build: Owner direction (2026-10-09): 'the world shell navigation should leverage the sun crystal menu nav and then every click after is the user moving another layer deep … the user moving through layers with more detail exposed against each object in the scene at each layer.' Today (src/components/WorldShell.jsx) the sun core (CRYSTAL_VARIANTS.signature, ~:259) only zooms out on click; islands come from resolveWorldIslands (src/lib/worldIslands.js); deeper levels are ad-hoc React state (focusedKey, atmosphereKey, selectedOpportunityId in useOpportunityPipeline, OpportunityOutputsSection's editor/historyOpen) with a separate '← Back to World' per level, returnKeyRef one level deep, no breadcrumb and no URL state (refresh loses place). Build ONE layer model, reusing what exists (no new 3D scene, no forked crystal variants — crystalGeometry.js rules): 1) Layer 0 = the sun: clicking the sun crystal opens the root menu — the islands presented around the sun as the menu (keyboard/screen-reader accessible list mirrored in the DOM), each labelled. 2) A useWorldLayers stack hook ({kind, key, label} per layer: island → atmosphere/moon or docked panel → item e.g. opportunity → sub-object e.g. output → version/editor) that every existing level pushes to instead of its own state; every click into an object pushes exactly one layer; the camera moves toward the selected object and the panel for that layer shows more detail about that object than the layer above (summary at the layer above, full detail + its child objects as clickable entries at its own layer). 3) A breadcrumb trail (Sun › island › item › sub-object) always visible in the World Shell; clicking a crumb pops to that layer; existing back buttons become 'pop one layer' (keep their labels working so world-shell-navigation's training spec still passes); Escape and browser Back pop one layer. 4) The stack is in the URL (/world?at=...) so refresh, Back/Forward and shared links restore the exact layer; unknown or no-longer-permitted entries fall back to the deepest valid layer with a visible note (never a blank screen). 5) Applies to members and admins, World / Journeys tabs (Journeys cards push the same layers), classic/embed views are layers too. Desktop and 390px (rail becomes a bottom sheet; crumbs wrap or collapse to '… › current' with the full trail one tap away). Reduced motion: camera cuts instead of flights. Training spec journeys must cover: sun menu → island → opportunity → output → version and back out by crumb, Back, Escape; refresh at depth; a deep link; member and admin; 390px. Fictional data only ('Northwind Freight', 'Principal Value Architect'). Change spec traces to docs/changes/world-shell-opportunity-outputs.md v1 and the island registry design in src/lib/worldIslands.js. BREADCRUMBS ARE THE PATH TAKEN (owner, 2026-10-09: 'i also need to be able to navigate back to the summary pages so i need breadcrumbs'): the trail records every layer the user actually passed through, including summary/list pages — the sun menu, the Journeys grid, an island's list view (e.g. the tracked-opportunities list), an outputs list, a version history — so every summary page is a clickable crumb that returns to it with its scroll position and filters intact. Opening the same object from a different summary page yields a different trail. Training spec must include: reach the same opportunity once via the sun menu and once via the Journeys grid and show each trail returns to the summary page it came from.

features.title: Live release tracker inside the Salt Basin platform: real-time trends, history slider, drill-down layers and numbered updates
features.build: Owner direction (2026-10-09): 'i want to rebuild this into my platform for real time updates in the salt basin website itself.' Port the release tracker (reference implementation: tools/release-tracker/index.html — its data rules, layers and validated chart palette are the spec; scripts/release-tracker-sync.mjs, release-history.mjs and release-update.mjs define the data shapes) into the platform as a real, live screen. REUSE FIRST: build on release-intelligence (release_* tables created lazily by releaseIntelligenceSchema.js, releaseLogImporter.js already reads tracker snapshots) and on the in-app release loop's screen if it is merged (never a second parallel release store). 1) INGEST, append-only (every snapshot kept, nothing overwritten, so history replays): (a) push — POST /api/release-tracker/snapshots with a per-release ingest token (generated, shown once, stored hashed, revocable in the UI) carrying the snapshot, history and updates JSON; (b) pull — because the agents' cloud container cannot reach saltbasin.net, the platform also fetches the committed files (docs/release-log/active-release.state.json, history.json, updates.json, active-release.features.json) from the configured public GitHub repo + branch, on a GitHub push webhook (HMAC-verified secret) and on a configurable poll interval as fallback. Repo, branch, interval, webhook secret and tokens are all edited in a Settings tab — no API-only configuration. 2) REAL TIME: a server-sent-events stream (/api/release-tracker/stream) notifies open viewers the moment a new snapshot lands; the client refetches and re-renders without a page reload, shows 'Updated N s ago' and a reconnecting state, and falls back to polling if the stream drops — never a silent stale screen. 3) UI reachable from the World Shell (an island/entry 'Release tracker'), rendered in the Salt Basin design language (brand.css tokens, Fraunces/Jost, light + dark): the overview trends panel (Show: Bugs / Test scores / Features passed; As: Totals / Change per update; Feature filter; legend toggles per series; as-of tiles with change vs previous update; time slider over every recorded state with update markers, prev/next-update and Live; the update note at the slider point; per-feature test-score sparklines; Table view), then the drill-down layers with path breadcrumbs (stat tile → list; feature → rounds, own bugs, backlog, agents; round → stages and bugs; bug → root cause, scope with evidence, history with commit links; agent → result, live test log, failures; status updates list → update detail with comparison). URL holds the path so refresh, Back and shared links restore it. Keep the validated chart colours (light #0B79A8,#B0661A,#9C4A8C,#4A8C2A; dark #2794C9,#C27C28,#B566A6,#6BA642), one axis per chart, hover tooltips, and the Table view. Use an existing chart approach in the repo (src/lib/careerCharts.js SVG helpers) or add chart.js as an npm dependency — not a CDN script. 4) ACCESS, configurable in Settings: admins always; selected members by email (e.g. a partner); optional read-only share link with a revocable token. Default admin-only. Bug/agent text shown to non-admin viewers is the same counts/labels-only data the snapshot already limits itself to. 5) The Claude Code side: extend scripts/release-tracker-sync.mjs (or a small companion script) with an optional push to the platform when PLATFORM_URL + an ingest token are set, logging (never hiding) a failed push. Training journeys must cover: ingest by pull with a fictional fixture repo state and by push with a token; a second ingest arriving while the screen is open updates it live without reload (SSE); slider back to an earlier state and Live; each toggle/filter; drill-down and breadcrumbs back to a summary page; access denied for a member not granted; share link view; revoked token rejected; 390px and dark mode. Fictional data only; this repo is public.
